Diony{{ls}}ius Areopagita is al for the Catholikes.}}This is that famous Denys that fir{{ls}}t conuerted France, and wrote tho{{ls}}e notable and diuine vvorkes ''de Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tica & cæle{{ls}}ti hierarchia, de diuinis nominibus'', and others, in vvhich he confirmeth and proueth plainely almo{{ls}}t al things that the Church now v{{ls}}eth in the mini{{ls}}tration of the holy Sacraments, and affirmeth that he learned them of the Apo{{ls}}tles, giuing al{{ls}}o te{{ls}}timonie for the Catholike faith in mo{{ls}}t things now controuer{{ls}}ed, {{ls}}o plainely, that our Aduer{{ls}}aries haue no {{ls}}hift but to deny this Denys to haue been the author of them, feyning that they be an others of later age. Vvhich is an old flight of Heretikes, but mo{{ls}}t proper to the{{ls}}e of al others. Who {{ls}}eeing al antiquitie again{{ls}}t them, are forced to be more bold or rather impudent then others in that point.

{{c|''At Corinth in Achaia, he worketh vvith his owne hands, preaching {{sc|Iesvs}} to be {{sc|Christ}}, vnto the Iewes vpon their Sabboths. 6 But they being ob{{ls}}tinate and bla{{ls}}pheming, he in plaine termes for{{ls}}aketh them, and turneth to the Gentils, among whom according to a vi{{ls}}ion that he had to embolden him, he planteth the Church in great numbers, 12 the ob{{ls}}tinat Iewes in vaine {{ls}}oliciting the Procon{{ls}}ul again{{ls}}t him. 18 From thence at length departing he returneth 19 by Ephe{{ls}}us (where he promi{{ls}}eth the Iewes to returne to them) 22 and {{ls}}o to Antioch in Syria (from whence he began his iourney Act. 15) 23 but not re{{ls}}ting, by and by he goeth againe to vi{{ls}}ite the new Churches that he planted Act. 16 in Galatia and Phrygia: 24 Apollo in his ab{{ls}}ence mightily confounding the Iewes at Ephe{{ls}}us, 27 and afterward at Corinth.''}}

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=1|align=float}}{{dropinitial|A}}{{sc|Fter}} the{{ls}}e things, departing from Athens, he came to Corinth. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=2|align=float}}† and finding a certaine Iew, named Aquila, borne in Pontus, vvho of late vvas come out of Italie, and Pri{{ls}}cilla his vvife (becau{{ls}}e Claudius had commaunded al Iewes to depart from Rome,) he came to them. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=3|align=float}}† And becau{{ls}}e he vvas of the {{ls}}ame craft, he remained with them, and wrought, (and they vvere tentmakers by their craft.) {{verse|chapter=18|verse=4|align=float}}† And<noinclude>{{continues|he}}
